name: Banyan Tree Higashiyama Kyoto
positioning: Hilltop hotel beside Kiyomizu-dera Temple in Kyoto, with natural hot spring baths, tatami-floored rooms and a Kengo Kuma-designed Bamboo Pavilion stage
best_for: Travelers who want natural hot spring bathing, including rooms with a private onsen
Guests interested in traditional Japanese performing arts such as Noh and geiko and maiko performances

facts.text: The hotel sits on a hill beside Kiyomizu-dera Temple, embraced by a bamboo forest.
The Bamboo Pavilion at the heart of the property was designed by architect Kengo Kuma and is a stage for classical performances.

The natural onsen is drawn from a hot spring on the hilltop grounds and can be enjoyed in the public bath with indoor and open-air pools, in select rooms with a private onsen, and in the spa's treatment suites.
Rooms have tatami mat floors and garden or city views, with wooden soaking bathtubs, sitting areas and separate walk-in showers.
Wellbeing Sanctuary King rooms have a private yoga space and floor-to-ceiling windows with city views.
The Banyan Onsen Retreat, described as the hotel's most luxurious sanctuary, has a private natural onsen.
The spa has natural hot springs and steam saunas.
The Onsen Indulgence treatment, exclusive to this spa, combines a private onsen experience with a full-body treatment.
The hotel has a bamboo garden of towering bamboo groves.
Geiko and maiko perform traditional dance with shamisen music against the backdrop of the hotel's Noh stage.
Ryozen, set beside the Bamboo Pavilion, offers kaiseki courses or counter dining with chefs cooking over the grill.
Ryozen SEN Bettei is a branch of Japanese Cuisine SEN serving creative kaiseki at a counter overlooking Higashiyama.

highlights.text: The Bamboo Pavilion, designed by Kengo Kuma, stands at the heart of the property as a stage for classical performances.
Onsen water comes from a natural hot spring on the hilltop grounds, used in the public bath with indoor and open-air pools, private in-room onsen and spa treatment suites.
Onsen Retreat rooms have a private natural onsen and look onto a Japanese courtyard garden.
The spa offers a private onsen experience in treatment rooms with traditional hinoki cypress bathtubs.
Noh performances are staged with masks illuminated by candlelight.

considerations.text: The nearest airport is Kansai International.
Valet parking is not available and parking reservations are not accepted.
WhataHotel notes the limited number of rooms may require booking in advance.
